To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a probabilistic model for merging outputs of classifiers improves the performance on the object detection task, and the performance is improved by training the classifiers on images from different sources.

(i) we propose a novel approach to merge the output of large margin classifiers; (ii) we show that this method is able to learn a probabilistically interpretable model that outperforms the single classifiers in the task of object detection; (iii) the proposed model is robust to changes in the data and it can be used in a wide variety of scenarios.

1) the proposed approach is effective to learn multimodal classification models; 2) a simple combination of classifiers is able to outperform the state-of-the-art in the task of urban cartography; 3) the proposed framework allows to learn multimodal models with a small number of samples, which is a desirable property for applications with limited training data.
